chapter: Emmett Hardy and the river towns
title: Owls Hall, the ferry landing and Jack Lane's trap drumming
summary: He describes rough dances across the river and the only time he saw Jack Lane play trap drums.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Well, this Owls Hall, it was just about a block down from the ferry landing. And they would do, if they caught you fooling, the fellas over there would go up the fellas from New Orleans fooling with any of the girls. Well, they'd do either one of two things. They'd either run them up the levee and down the ferry landing. If the ferry wasn't in, don't stop, just keep going, you know. Either that or the two fellas would get the guy, one by the arms and one by the legs and take him by a window like that and swing him like that. It was built on pilings right on the water, you see. And they'd swing him like that and right out the window they'd throw him. Either that or they'd run him down to where the automobiles, the horse and wagons went in those days down the ferry. If the ferry wasn't there, just keep going, don't stop unless you want to get, you know, really clubbed up. And then when the fellas on this side would catch those guys from over there coming over here with it, same thing. They'd talk about juvenile delinquency. And that was just, that was a common occurrence. At all dances and things like that. Another place over there they call it the Babies Hall that they used to do a lot of. That's where Jack Lane played. He played the Babies Hall and he played another place over there called the Fireman's Hall in Harley. That's the only time I ever saw Jack play double drums. Not double drums, I mean play trap drums. And it was only four pieces. It was he and Abbie Brunnis. And I can't, no piano. See what I think it was, uh, cornet, drums, bass, no other guitar, banjo. But that, that, that kind of combination. And that's the only time I ever saw the old man play trap drums. But he mostly, mostly his, his work mostly was parades, picnics, things like that. But this was regular.
